<!-- factory-judge-review round=2 -->
### Factory judge · round 2 · approve

#### Acceptance
- A1: met — The flaky-under-load test asserts that tests.pass passes, the verdict passes, and the flaky note is recorded.
- A2: met — The test asserts a fail, exit code 1, both FAIL outputs kept, and the real-failure note.
- A3: met — The stand-in's argv log shows one full run, then one call per failing file. This is only verified against the stand-in; see the suggestion on `--`.
- A4: met — `reportOnFailure: true` is set and asserted, and the floor reads the full run's summary after a failing test.
- A5: met — The diff only adds flaky-under-load.test.ts; no test file that existed at base is touched.

<details><summary>4 suggestion(s), non-blocking</summary>

- The git project still runs alongside the unit project `vitest.workspace.ts:26` — Order the projects, for example with `sequence: { groupOrder: 1 }` on the git project and `0` on unit (vitest 3), or run the git project in a second `vitest run --project git` step. Then make the changeset text match.
- Check that the `--` separator reaches vitest as intended `packages/runtime/src/judge/tier1.ts:605` — Add a test that runs the real `pnpm run test` re-run against one file, or build the argument list per package manager (for pnpm, no `--`).
- Clearing flaky files doesn't refresh coverage in repos without reportOnFailure `packages/runtime/src/judge/tier1.ts:379` — When every file clears and the coverage control is red for a missing summary, run the tests and coverage controls once more, or note in the verdict that the floor couldn't be read.
- Mixed outcomes leave out the files that passed alone `packages/runtime/src/judge/tier1.ts:390` — Push the flaky-under-load note for each `alone` entry with `ok: true` in both branches.

</details>

_Not reviewed: `packages/action/dist/SOURCE_SHA256` (generated), `packages/action/dist/index.js` (generated)._

suggestions.title: The git project still runs alongside the unit project
suggestions.detail: `singleFork` only makes the git-heavy files run one at a time among themselves. Vitest still schedules the `unit` and `git` projects concurrently. The git files therefore keep contending with the rest of the suite, which is the load the card asks to remove. The changeset's claim that they run "one at a time after the rest of the suite" is inaccurate. The tier 1 re-run covers the symptom, but the first half of the card is only partly done. Also, on vitest 3.2+ `defineWorkspace` is deprecated and prints a warning.
suggestions.repro: Run `pnpm run test` on a loaded Windows machine. store.test.ts in the `git` fork runs while the `unit` forks are busy, so it can still hit the 30s timeout.
suggestions.fix: Order the projects, for example with `sequence: { groupOrder: 1 }` on the git project and `0` on unit (vitest 3), or run the git project in a second `vitest run --project git` step. Then make the changeset text match.

suggestions.title: Check that the `--` separator reaches vitest as intended
suggestions.detail: `rerunAlone` appends `--`, `--coverage.enabled=false` and the file to the detected command. In this repo that command is `pnpm run test`. pnpm 7+ can forward the `--` to the script. If it does, vitest's cac parser puts both the filter and the coverage flag into `options['--']`. The result would be a whole-suite re-run with coverage on, which breaks A3 in practice and rewrites coverage-summary.json. The A3 unit test can't catch this because the stand-in drops every argument starting with `--`.
suggestions.repro: Run the re-run command by hand in this repo: `pnpm run test -- --coverage.enabled=false packages/engine/src/paths.test.ts`. See whether vitest runs one file or all of them.
suggestions.fix: Add a test that runs the real `pnpm run test` re-run against one file, or build the argument list per package manager (for pnpm, no `--`).

suggestions.title: Clearing flaky files doesn't refresh coverage in repos without reportOnFailure
suggestions.detail: tier1 runs in every factory repo, not only this one. The old whole-suite retry re-ran coverage too. The new path flips tests.pass to pass but leaves `quality.coverage.floor` as the full run left it. With vitest's default `reportOnFailure: false`, the failed run wrote no summary, so the floor stays red and the round still fails.
suggestions.repro: Take a factory repo whose vitest config has coverage on and no reportOnFailure. One file times out in the suite and passes alone. tests.pass becomes pass, coverage.floor is red with "wrote no" coverage summary, and the verdict is fail.
suggestions.fix: When every file clears and the coverage control is red for a missing summary, run the tests and coverage controls once more, or note in the verdict that the floor couldn't be read.

suggestions.title: Mixed outcomes leave out the files that passed alone
suggestions.detail: When some files fail alone and others pass alone, only the real failures get a note. Nothing records which files were flaky under load.
suggestions.repro: Suite fails A and B, and only B fails alone. The notes name B as a real failure and say nothing about A.
suggestions.fix: Push the flaky-under-load note for each `alone` entry with `ok: true` in both branches.
